question: A shopkeeper, on selling a pan for ₹10, loses (1)/(11) of what it cost him. The cost price of a pan is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

According to the question, **Loss** = 1/11 of **Cost Price (CP)**.

This implies the ratio **CP : Loss** = 11 : 1.

Therefore, **Selling Price (SP)** = CP − Loss = 11 − 1 = 10 units.

Given **Selling Price** = ₹10. ⇒ 10 units = ₹10 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹1.

**Cost Price** = 11 units = 11 × ₹1 = ₹11.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Selling Price (SP)** of the pan = ₹10

**Loss** = 1/11 of **Cost Price (CP)**

**Formula Used:**

**Cost Price (CP)** = **Selling Price (SP)** + **Loss**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f323cdbfb09753b3d6543a064e58cebbe9f4391a83578d0b63dba8cefe139461.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Cost Price** of the pan be ₹x.

⇒ **Loss** = x/11

⇒ **Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price** − **Loss**

⇒ 10 = x − (x / 11)

⇒ 10 = (11x − x) / 11

⇒ 10 = 10x / 11

⇒ 1 = x / 11

⇒ x = 11

**∴ The correct answer is ₹11.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss Percentage Formula

**Loss%** = (**Loss** ÷ **Cost Price**) × 100. In this case, **Loss%** = (1/11) × 100 ≈ 9.09%.

Relation between SP and CP during Loss

**Selling Price (SP)** = **Cost Price (CP)** × (100 − **Loss%**) ÷ 100.

Calculating CP from Loss Fraction

If **Loss** is 1/n of **CP**, then **CP** = **SP** × [n ÷ (n − 1)]. Here, n = 11, so **CP** = 10 × (11/10) = 11.
